input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes a most-favoured-nation obligation on us, not the Vendor: before engaging another provider we would have to disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive. The obligation is open-ended — no defined product, no time limit, and no like-for-like comparison carve-outs — so it fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory. It also contradicts Section 12.3, which recites that "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." We therefore move to the preferred position by removing the obligation, which also resolves the internal conflict with Section 12.3.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.

proposal.summary: Remove the Customer-side MFN/match obligation in Section 7.2
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a most-favoured-nation obligation running against us, so we have removed the requirement to disclose and match third-party offers in Section 7.2; this also aligns with Section 12.3, which confirms we give no most-favoured-customer commitment. Vendor-granted MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.

ops.oldText: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
ops.newText: Customer is not required to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
